named_questions: Does existing gate-set independence already provide the exact dimension-independent, collapse-sensitive persistent-feedback modulus?
What prior conditional-copy continuity prevents a first-principle novelty claim?
Under which input and gate-set assumptions does precision imply efficient compilation?

sources.inspected: Sections 2-5: model, local fixed/decreasing power comparisons, metric, query frontiers, preparation robustness and general precision caveat
sources.transfer: Complete normalized history blocks and identical operations on matching histories enable the single-gate insertion. Sections 3-6 rederive the local comparisons and compose at ordinary-gate frontiers.
sources.finding: The new modulus is a direct auxiliary consequence of retained P011 machinery; its earlier preparation bound covered a particular construction.

sources.source: Aaronson, Bouland, Fitzsimons, Lee: The space just above BQP
sources.inspected: Model and Appendix D gate-set-independence comparison
sources.transfer: Fixed submitted circuit and Markov/history coupling establish ideal PDQP gate-set independence.
sources.finding: Displayed dimension factor 2^(2 ell+1) and accuracy 2^(-ell^2 T-10); exponentially small error still needs polynomial accuracy bits. This statement does not give the immediate-feedback, collapse-sensitive square-root modulus.

sources.inspected: Appendix D, printed pages 20-22; naCQP label and fixed-circuit contract
sources.finding: Retains a dimension-dependent gate-set-independence proof, not the full persistent-feedback contract.

sources.source: Dawson and Nielsen: The Solovay-Kitaev algorithm
sources.inspected: Section 2 Definition 1 and Theorem 1, Section 3 algorithm; fixed SU(d), universal inverse-closed finite gate set
sources.transfer: Constant local dimension and effective gate descriptions allow precision to be converted into polynomial compilation/synthesis costs; arbitrary growing-width real matrices do not have this structure automatically.
sources.finding: Compilation is inherited. Explicit E/S/L costs include description evaluation, finite arithmetic and printing the complete synthesized word.

sources.source: Cakan et al.: On the Cryptographic Futility of Non-Collapsing Measurements
sources.inspected: Definition 8.1, Section 8.2 Claim 8.3 (equation 156), its three intermediate-state comparisons (157-170), Markov comparison (150)
sources.transfer: Two-time conditional-copy states in a fixed ideal circuit admit trace-distance control. The present proof instead uses P011 powered histories for the collapse-sensitive all-feedback contract.
sources.finding: TD(A_tilde,B_tilde)<=3 TD(A,B) already gives dimension-independent conditional-copy continuity. Do not claim this general continuity principle is new. The inspected claim does not itself state the target sqrt(K) bound.
sources.limitation: No full cryptographic theorem audit or exhaustive priority claim.

sources.inspected: Narrow oracle-model and continuity-term check only
sources.finding: Model-scope check; no absence-of-prior-work conclusion follows from this limited inspection.

classification: Attributed auxiliary mathematical consequence of P011; internal analytical proof, not established field novelty or independent/formal certification.
limitations: Targeted primary-text comparison, not exhaustive novelty research or validation of entire cited papers. Source hashes identify locally inspected bytes; third-party full texts are not redistributed.
decision: Close the bounded precision obligation; SELECTION NONE for successor and no automatic publication.
